title: How to Use the Shift Scheduler in Project P.I.T.T.
h1: How to Use the Shift Scheduler in Project P.I.T.T.
quickAnswer: The Shift Scheduler is a built-in, full-release automation tool in Project P.I.T.T. used to release items in timed or batch patterns for controlled automation lanes and for x300 combo setups once a lane is tested. Connect it to the devices you want to control (fans, magnets, remote outputs or batch-release endpoints) and place it in your Automation flow; be aware that remote usage and timed/batch behavior are different ways to operate it, and recent version fixes mean you should treat current-version behavior as the baseline. If it seems not to work, check connectivity, mode (remote vs batch), and whether the lane was validated before relying on x300 combos; the scheduler does not guarantee a combo.
description:
What the Shift Scheduler is
The Shift Scheduler is a current full-release automation tool in Project P.I.T.T. that schedules controlled releases or shifts of items in an automation lane. It belongs in the Automation category and is typically used between other automation modules; the intended information architecture is Automation → Shift Scheduler → x300 Combo, with Trade Terminal and Panel Rack mentioned as neighboring automation tools you may use nearby.
How to use it (high level)
- Place the Shift Scheduler in your automation lane once the lane logic is tested. It is intended to manage timed or batched releases rather than inventing lane behavior for you.
- Connect its outputs to the devices that perform the physical action in your lane: fans, magnets, or remote-controlled release endpoints are commonly discussed by players. The scheduler can drive remote outputs or serve as a batch-release controller depending on mode.
- Use it for controlled automation lanes and for x300 combo setups only after you have tested the lane; the scheduler helps sequence releases but does not guarantee a successful combo on its own.
What to connect
- Fans and magnets are frequently connected to a Shift Scheduler to control airflow or magnetic release in lanes. Remote outputs are also commonly used when the scheduler must trigger distant hardware or a different panel.
- Trade Terminal and Panel Rack are neighboring tools in Automation you may pair with the scheduler when building a complete line; think of the scheduler as the timing/batching element within that environment.
Remote usage vs timed/batch behavior
- Player discussion distinguishes remote usage (triggering distant outputs or other modules) from local timed or batch behavior (releasing sets of items on a schedule). Decide whether you need remote triggers or local batch releases and wire the scheduler accordingly.
- Timed and batch modes change how releases are grouped and dispatched; because behavior can differ, use the current-version behavior as the baseline when designing your lane.
Automation and x300 combo use
- The scheduler is useful for controlled lanes and for x300 combo setups after the lane is validated. It sequences releases for higher-level combo strategies but does not itself guarantee a combo will succeed.
Common reasons it seems not to work
- Incorrect or missing connections to the devices (fans, magnets, remote outputs).
- Using an untested lane: timing or batch settings that work in isolation can fail in the full lane until the lane is validated.
- Confusing remote triggers with local batch behavior; ensure the scheduler is set and wired for the intended mode.
- Expectation mismatches with earlier versions: prior inconsistencies were fixed in recent updates, so some older community assumptions no longer apply.
Current-version behavior
- Recent version changes resolved earlier inconsistencies; use the current release behavior as your baseline when building and debugging. Don’t rely on pre-fix assumptions about how the scheduler behaved.
FAQ
Q: Will the Shift Scheduler guarantee an x300 combo?
A: No. It can help sequence releases for x300 combos after lanes are tested, but it does not guarantee success.
Q: Should I wire fans or magnets directly to the scheduler?
A: Fans and magnets are common endpoints to control from the scheduler; ensure correct connections and test the lane first.
Q: What’s the difference between remote and batch modes?
A: Remote usage triggers distant outputs or other modules; batch/timed behavior groups releases locally. Choose the mode that matches your lane architecture.
Q: Where does Shift Scheduler live in the tool hierarchy?
A: It sits in Automation and is used with nearby tools like the Trade Terminal and Panel Rack; for combo work the intended flow is Automation → Shift Scheduler → x300 Combo.
If you need deeper troubleshooting, review connections to fans, magnets and remote outputs, validate the lane in isolation, and treat the current-version behavior as authoritative when comparing to older community notes.
